Standards, research, and use

Designed for NC grades 3–5 mathematics. The new grade 3 and 5 examples were checked against the accessible DPI June 2019 unpacking documents. Grade 4 computation limits in these examples follow the accessible NC unpacking: three-digit by one-digit multiplication, two-digit by two-digit multiplication, and three-digit by one-digit division. Current direct DPI downloads were unavailable when checked on October 1, 2026; consult the current unpacking hub for later updates. Verify local pacing and any later state updates.

Content charts are original worked examples. Practices charts and classroom routines are labeled separately. Chart 21 and equal-group portions of Chart 13 provide prerequisite support. These charts are not an assessment, complete curriculum, or evidence that anchor charts alone improve achievement. Teach and build them with students; explicitly connect models, words, and symbols.

Marker colors distinguish labeled quantities, highlight important relationships, and identify checks or removed parts. White space separates ideas; the mathematical models determine each chart’s layout. Labels and equations carry the meaning too. Arrow keys flip charts while focus is outside a form control.
